question: Why do atoms typically form chemical bonds with each other?

options.A: To decrease the temperature of the surrounding fluid
options.B: To convert protons directly into neutrons
options.C: To achieve a stable, full outer electron shell
options.D: To increase their overall physical mass

explanation: Atoms interact chemically because a complete outer electron shell provides maximum stability. [learn more](BMP113_U1_T3#BMP113_U1_T3_h1)

question: Why is studying chemical bonding useful for student midwives?

options.A: It teaches how to safely deliver a baby feet-first
options.B: It measures the exact weight of a newborn infant
options.C: It explains how body fluids and medicines function
options.D: It calculates the proper dosage of herbal teas

explanation: Chemical bonding principles form the foundation for understanding electrolytes, fluid balance, and pharmacology in clinical care. [learn more](BMP113_U1_T3#BMP113_U1_T3_h1)

question: How are electrons handled during the formation of an ionic bond?

options.A: They are completely transferred from one atom to another
options.B: They are converted directly into atomic protons
options.C: They are destroyed to release thermal energy
options.D: They are shared equally between two non-metal atoms

explanation: Ionic bonding involves a permanent transfer of electrons, unlike covalent bonding where electrons are shared. [learn more](BMP113_U1_T3#BMP113_U1_T3_h2)

question: What force holds an ionic compound together after an electron transfer happens?

options.A: Physical friction between neighboring cell walls
options.B: Surface tension from surrounding water molecules
options.D: Magnetic pull from the Earth's core

explanation: Positive ions and negative ions pull toward each other due to standard rules of electrostatic attraction. [learn more](BMP113_U1_T3#BMP113_U1_T3_h2)

question: What is the term for a positively charged ion?
explanation: A cation is formed when an atom loses electrons, resulting in a net positive charge. [learn more](BMP113_U1_T3#BMP113_U1_T3_h3)

question: Why does an atom become negatively charged when it turns into an anion?

options.A: It has absorbed extra heat from the bloodstream
options.B: It has shared its nucleus with a neighboring cell
options.C: It has accepted extra electrons carrying negative charges
options.D: It has lost all of its original heavy protons

explanation: Anions gain extra electrons, increasing the negative particle count relative to positive protons. [learn more](BMP113_U1_T3#BMP113_U1_T3_h3)

question: Which property is typical of ionic compounds when they are dissolved in water?

options.A: They turn completely into solid plastic
options.C: They prevent any chemical reactions from occurring
options.D: They repel all surrounding water molecules

explanation: Dissolved ionic compounds separate into free ions, allowing an electrical current to pass through the solution. [learn more](BMP113_U1_T3#BMP113_U1_T3_h4)

question: Why do ionic compounds generally have high melting points?

options.A: Strong electrostatic forces hold the ions tightly together
options.B: Water molecules freeze inside the crystal structure
options.C: Their outer electrons refuse to move under any condition
options.D: They contain large amounts of trapped air bubbles

explanation: Breaking apart the rigid crystal lattice requires significant thermal energy to overcome the ionic attraction. [learn more](BMP113_U1_T3#BMP113_U1_T3_h4)

question: Which electrolyte is found in the highest concentration outside of human cells?
explanation: Sodium is the principal extracellular cation responsible for maintaining fluid balance and blood volume. [learn more](BMP113_U1_T3#BMP113_U1_T3_h5)

question: A pregnant woman in labor is losing fluids and needs intravenous support. Which key intracellular electrolyte must be managed carefully to protect her heart rhythm?
explanation: Potassium is the primary intracellular ion that directly governs cardiac muscle stability and electrical rhythm. [learn more](BMP113_U1_T3#BMP113_U1_T3_h5)

question: What term describes a dangerously low level of sodium in the blood?
explanation: Hyponatremia is defined by a deficit of sodium ions in the extracellular fluid. [learn more](BMP113_U1_T3#BMP113_U1_T3_h6)

question: Why are abnormal potassium levels particularly dangerous for a patient?

options.A: They disrupt the electrical rhythm of the heart
options.B: They stop the liver from producing red blood cells
options.C: They immediately cause total hair loss
options.D: They turn the skin completely yellow

explanation: Potassium governs cellular electrical stability, and imbalances can trigger life-threatening heart arrhythmias. [learn more](BMP113_U1_T3#BMP113_U1_T3_h6)
